A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ICRT study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial appendix shortening.

before.justification: V1 reports original ICRT attack results, harmfulness rankings, concept-count sensitivity experiments, and NeurIPS Red Teaming evaluation results. Baseline scores are separately attributed to prior work.

after.justification: V2 retains original ICRT experiments and harmfulness rankings and reports a DeepSeek-R1 result in its NeurIPS evaluation table.

M1.justification: The two-stage ICRT procedure, iterative concept selection and reassembly, multi-model voting, and three ranking algorithms remain unchanged. Removing model-specific implementation descriptions does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate jailbreak attacks on AdvBench's 520 harmful objectives and the NeurIPS 2024 Red Teaming Track, retaining the same five harmfulness categories. Target-model substitutions do not introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and the harmfulness-ranking figures, including GCG-T/PAIR for black-box comparisons and GCG/AutoDAN for white-box comparisons. Newly cited attacks are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The NeurIPS target set replaces Llama2-7B with DeepSeek-R1. Appendix C.4 changes defense evaluation from rejection strings plus a HarmBench judge and manual conflict resolution to rejection strings plus manual verification. Section 4.1 changes Qwen-7B-chat to Qwen2-7B, although other labels retain Qwen-7B-chat. These are reported setting changes; reruns are not established.

E4.justification: V2 removes the government-database intrusion case in B.1, human validation of intent recognition in C.1, and Figure 7's extended sensitivity results, including k = 3, 5, and 10. Main Figure 3, defense tests, and ranking-consistency comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The multi-judge majority-voting approach is retained; the removed human-agreement percentage is a validation result rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V1 Table 5's Llama2-7B result of 62% ASR is removed, while v2 Table 4 adds DeepSeek-R1 at 96%; the other five entries are unchanged. Tables 1–3 remain identical, including ICRT's 98.2% average. V2 also removes the above-99% human-agreement finding and extended concept-count results.

T1.justification: Appendix E removes the explicit Rank Centrality transition-matrix construction from positive entries of the comparison matrix, retaining its generic weighted-graph formulation. The main equations, BTL assumptions, and HodgeRank mathematical treatment remain; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a psychology-inspired ICRT jailbreak method and a ranking-based harmfulness metric extending binary success evaluation. The introduction's three contributions and the conclusion's effectiveness claims retain the same meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Appendix D removes interpretations that Llama2-7B has stronger safety mechanisms and that higher-capacity models handle decomposition more consistently than smaller models. The central cognitive explanations, k = 6 tradeoff, ranking-quality caveats, and societal-risk discussion remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link but removes substantial evaluation documentation: the named GPT-4/fine-tuned GPT-4o/o1 judging ensemble and Appendix C.6's training-data description, compliance labels, JSONL format, and 10-epoch fine-tuning specification. It also removes the classification prompt and GPT-3.5 identification for decomposition and concept selection. These are documentation losses, not demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including DrAttack, Pandora, intention-analysis defense, and Ma et al. (2021), and replaces the Albers–de Vries Elo reference with Elo (2008). The related-work organization and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged; numerous other reference edits update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. V2 makes local wording and terminology edits, updates affiliations and conference front matter, adds acknowledgements, and condenses appendix explanations by removing several explanatory subsections and repetitive passages.

P2.justification: V2 removes the policy-comparison table, numerical Elo table, and extended radar Figure 7. The retained Figure 6 still plots the Elo-table results, and its caption corrects the display offset from 1500 to 1000. Main Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–5 retain their designs; appendix placement changes.

improvement.justification: The code-access pointer, DeepSeek-R1 result, and Figure 6 caption correction are useful additions. However, removing judge identities and fine-tuning specifications makes the central harmfulness evaluation less reproducible from the paper, while supplementary validation is reduced. With the main results and claims unchanged, these documentation losses outweigh the limited additions and editorial gains.
